title: What is an immaculate inning? Red Sox’s Payton Tolle just threw one against the Royals
content:
BOSTON — The Boston Red Sox and Kansas Royals had to wait through a nearly two-hour rain delay Sunday, but when the game finally arrived, it came with a treat in the top of the first inning: an immaculate inning from Red Sox starter Payton Tolle.

Tolle fired nine straight strikes — eight of which were increasingly harder four-seamers — to strike out Nick Loftin, Bobby Witt Jr. and Jac Caglianone in the top of the first.

Tolle got seven swings and misses through the first nine pitches. The only two pitches that weren’t: a called third strike to Loftin and a foul ball against a sinker to Caglianone.

On the precipice of the unique feat, having thrown eight straight strikes, the ever-affable Tolle cracked a smile on the mound before firing a 97.9 mph four-seamer past Caglianone.

Tolle spun around the back of the mound and pumped his fist triumphantly as catcher Adley Rutschman ran to the mound for an embrace.

It marked the fifth immaculate inning in the majors this season, but just the eighth in Red Sox history and the first since Chris Sale did so on Aug. 26, 2021.

Meanwhile, it was just the second time a Red Sox pitcher has thrown an immaculate inning in the first inning. The other pitcher? Pedro Martínez on May 18, 2002, against Seattle.

On Saturday, Sunday’s game that was originally scheduled for 1:35 p.m. was pushed back to a 3:05 p.m. start time due to heavy rain.

Tolle, who ended up pitching six scoreless innings in a 4-1 Red Sox win, was evidently unfazed by the weather delay.
